punchline: At his lowest point, William James gave himself one year of acting as if he were 100 percent responsible for everything in his life.
thirty_sec: Around 1872 William James's life was falling apart and he'd thought about suicide. One night, reading Charles Peirce, he made a deal: for one year he'd believe he was fully responsible for everything that happened to him and do all he could to change it. If nothing improved, he'd accept he was powerless. He later called it his rebirth. Mark Manson explains it with a baby left on your doorstep: not your fault, but your call.
